global_rules.map_rule: Never shade a municipal polygon as submerged using a tide-gauge value, one-degree grid, county planning range, or broader study-domain total.
global_rules.language_rule: Use observed, projected, scenario, planning range, exposed, displaced, and migrated as distinct labels.
global_rules.adaptation_rule: Place included and excluded defenses next to the title, not only in a tooltip.
global_rules.boundary_rule: Display the exact geographic boundary or point used by the source.
global_rules.precision_rule: Retain source precision; do not interpolate between decadal scenarios for animation unless explicitly labeled as visualization-only.

charts.title: Local relative sea-level scenarios
required_controls: 30 N / 90 W grid near New Orleans
annotations: Relative sea level combines ocean and land motion.
Grand Isle is not New Orleans.
The one-degree New Orleans grid is not a parcel-depth map.

charts.title: Observed relative sea-level trends
annotations: Station records start in different years.
Do not extrapolate the linear trend as a forecast.

charts.title: Days per year above local flood thresholds
constraints: A projected threshold day does not imply an entire city floods.
Show saturation at 365 rather than drawing beyond the physical maximum.

charts.title: How rising water can erode urban habitability before permanent inundation
Land motion changes 2050 coastal exposure
charts.required_subtitle: SSP2-4.5; static connected-inundation exposure; 2010 people/property baseline; defended and undefended results are not interchangeable.
prohibited: renaming the Miami study domain City of Miami
portraying New Orleans undefended exposure as observed floodwater

charts.title: Miami-Dade sea-level planning range
charts.required_subtitle: Inches above 2000 mean sea level at the Key West reference; adopted planning range, not uniform flood depth or probability interval.
prohibited: overlay on a parcel map as water depth
comparison to NOAA change-since-2020 without baseline conversion

charts.title: Where U.S. sea-level migration could redistribute population under a high-end 2100 scenario
charts.required_subtitle: Modeled net migration under 1.8 m sea-level rise by 2100; scenario stress test, not a destination forecast.

charts.title: Sea-level milestones used in a county migration model
charts.required_subtitle: Dates are from Robinson et al.'s study scenarios and are not NOAA local projections or city-loss dates.
prohibited: combining medium and high scenario points

charts.title: Arrivals and receiving-system capacity
prohibited: one composite overload score without component units
assuming each migrant creates identical demand

charts.title: Protect, accommodate, avoid, restore, or relocate
prohibited: fixed retirement year without a source
calling any single measure a complete solution
